To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The measured particle ratios in Au–Au collisions at RHIC energies can be described within a chemical and temperature dependent chiral SU( 3 ) σ–ω approach, but not in a free hadron gas calculation.”

the measured particle ratios in the central heavy-ion collisions can not be described in a simple noninteracting hadron gas model, and that the chemical freeze-out temperatures and the effective hadron masses are strongly reduced in the medium.

the chemical and thermal freeze-out temperatures in central Au–Au collisions at RHIC are lower by 35 Me V than those predicted by non-interacting hadron gas models, and that the in-medium effective hadron masses are lower by 100–150 Me V than the corresponding vacuum masses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for signals of chiral symmetry breaking in particle ratios at RHIC-BNH.
the question of whether the measured particle ratios in heavy-ion collisions at the RHIC-BNL can be explained by a chiral phase-transition scenario.
the question whether or not the particle ratios measured in central heavy ion collisions at RHIC indicate the occurrence of a chiral phase in the medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a chemical freeze-out temperature of 170 MeV and in-medium masses are needed for a consistent description of the measured particle ratios in Au+Au collisions at RHIC.
a chiral phase is present at RHIC, but that it is not reached in chemical freeze-out.
the data at RHIC are consistent with a chiral phase of QCD matter, which, however, does not show up in the measured hadron abundances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the measured particle ratios in the central region of the collisions at RHIC indicate that the hadron masses are reduced in the medium, but do not provide evidence for a chiral phase-transition.

the measured particle ratios in the most central heavy-ion collisions are in good agreement with a chirally broken phase at the chemical freeze-out, which is characterized by a temperature and density dependent in-medium hadron mass and a modified chemical potential.

the measured particle ratios in heavy-ion collisions at the highest RHIC energies can only be understood if one takes into account the in-medium properties of the hadrons, i.e. the effective masses and effective chemical potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hadron ratios in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC are sensitive to the chiral properties of the medium and can be used to extract effective hadron masses at high temperatures and densities.
the particle ratios measured at RHIC are not a good thermometer to measure the chiral phase boundary.
the measured hadron yields are the result of a complicated dynamical process, which is not captured by simple noninteracting hadronic gas calculations.
